# Five New Google Photos Updates for Organizing and Sharing Holiday Memories

> **In short:** Google says five recent Google Photos updates can help you turn holiday photos into highlight albums, filter shared albums by people or pets, quickly find faces, tidy your Collections tab, and make gifts. Google published the announcement on November 23, 2026.

Holiday season means hundreds of photos from a single weekend, and most of us never get around to sorting them. If that sounds familiar, you're not alone. Google's latest Google Photos changes aim to cut down on the sorting so you can spend more time enjoying the moments.

## Turning a holiday into a story

A **highlight album** is a short collection that Google Photos builds from a set of pictures, so you don't have to pick each one by hand. Google's example is a Thanksgiving dinner: you create a highlight album of the celebration, send the link to family by email, and add a short written recap of the day.

Google also mentions 12 new **Remix templates**. A Remix template is a ready-made design you drop your photos into. Google says you can use them to make scrapbook-style holiday cards or pastel illustrations from your festive shots. The post doesn't spell out every step, so think of the templates as a starting point you can explore inside the app.

## Finding people and pets faster

If you share albums with relatives, you know how much scrolling a shared album can take. Google says you can now filter shared albums by people or pets, so you see only the photos of the person or dog you're looking for.

Google also says that tapping any face in the scrolling row at the top of the screen shows you photos of that person. This works for yourself, loved ones, or pets. It's a quick way to find every photo of Grandma from the year's gatherings.

## Making your Collections tab work for you

The **Collections tab** is where Google Photos groups your albums and memories. Google says you can pin your favorite albums and memories so they appear first, and hide the ones you rarely open. Think of it like rearranging the shelf by your front door: the things you use most go where you can reach them.

On Android phones, Google says you can open local media, meaning photos saved directly on your device, through a option labeled "On this device." This helps if you want to find a photo you took on your phone before it was backed up.

## Turning photos into gifts

Google says you can create photo books, blankets, mugs, and similar keepsakes through the Fujifilm for Google Photos Print Store, a partner store linked from the app. Check the store's own pages for current options and pricing before you order.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you want to share the holidays with family, a highlight album plus a short recap is an easy way to send everyone the same story.
- **For your business or work**: Teams that keep shared photo albums for events or company parties can use the people and pet filters to find specific images faster.
- **If you're just getting started**: Begin with one album. Pin it to the top of your Collections tab so you can find it quickly next time.
- **If you already use it**: Pin your most-used albums, then hide the rest. You can revisit the Remix templates to turn a favorite shot into a card for someone who doesn't use social media.

## Wrap-up

Google says these updates are meant to reduce the time you spend managing photos, so you can focus on the memories themselves. The post doesn't list every plan or device that gets each feature, so check your own app to see what's available to you. Your next step: open Google Photos today, pick one holiday moment, and try building a highlight album for it.
